subject: Post-call recap: priorities, pilot scope & provisioning asks
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Ross <emma@edgescale.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-14T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: priorities, pilot scope & provisioning asks

Hi Emma / Sam — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a suggested 30-day pilot plan to validate performance + cost controls. Please read through and flag anything you want adjusted.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Latency spikes during burst traffic causing tail latency above acceptable SLAs (customer-facing inference).
- Unpredictable per-token cost with current provider and lack of visibility by route/model.
- Compliance needs: SOC2 audit coming Q4, strict egress/ingress controls, and longer-term requirement for VPC/private deployments.

High-level pilot scope (proposed):
- Duration: 30 days (evaluation window + one-week buffer).
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated (us-west region) — reserved capacity (2x A100-equivalent) for predictable throughput.
- Model: Open-model variant we've benchmarked (quantized) — we'll bring a compatible variant if you have a model preference.
- Workload: Subset of production request logs (anonymized) + 3 prioritized prompt families (customer search, conversational support, reranking).
- Success metrics (baseline -> target):
  - P99 inference latency: current baseline 1.2s -> target < 600ms
  - Unit token cost: baseline unknown -> goal <$0.002/token (target to be refined after 1 week)
  - Quality: eval accuracy / NDCG improvement vs baseline >= 5% on your labeled set (we'll use the prompt eval suite).

Owners / roles (proposed):
- EdgeScale: Emma (product lead), Sam (platform/network)
- Redwood: Lukas (AE, program owner), Karthik (solutions engineering, access + runbooks), Irene (CS lead, evals + success criteria), Soojin (security adviser — will triage questions with your security ops)

Immediate asks from EdgeScale to unblock pilot:
1) Provide a 72-hour window for VPN/allowlist IP provisioning (attach network-allowlist.txt we reference below).
2) Short anonymized samples of request logs for prompt tuning (SFTP/secure transfer preferred).
3) SOC2 questionnaire if available — we can start with what you have and exchange evidence during the pilot.

Attachments (stubs):
- edgescale-security-questionnaire.pdf (requested)
- pilot-metrics-template.xlsx (we'll populate baseline + targets)
- network-allowlist.txt (egress/ingress IP ranges we'd use)

Proposed near-term timeline (we can shift based on provisioning lead time):
- Day 0 (this week): Kickoff call + access requests submitted
- Week 1: Environment provisioned, initial prompt set ingestion, baseline run
- Week 2: Iterations, targeted quantization/latency tuning, start evals
- Week 3: Cost tuning, batching/caching configs, quality regressions check
- Week 4: Final acceptance demo + recommendations for production rollout or Dedicated->Private path

Next steps: could we lock a 45-minute kickoff for Tuesday or Thursday next week? If you prefer, Karthik can run a shorter ops-only session for the network/allowlist work.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a one-pager and populate the pilot metrics sheet with the targets we discussed.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: pilot-metrics-template.xlsx (stub), edgescale-security-questionnaire.pdf (stub), network-allowlist.txt (stub)
From: Emma Ross <emma@edgescale.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Jensen <sam.jensen@edgescale.com>
Date: 2027-06-14T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: priorities, pilot scope & provisioning asks

Thanks Lukas — good write-up. Confirmation and a few clarifications below.

Confirming pain/context:
- Latency spikes: yes — mostly during peak search periods (roughly 10:30-11:30am PT and 3:00-4:00pm PT).
- Cost: we've seen big variance across models/over time; visibility is limited.
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II in process (target Q4). We must make sure no unapproved egress paths are used.

We can provide:
- A 48-hour anonymized sample of request logs via SFTP (I'll have ops ship this by tomorrow EOD).
- Sam will handle IP/VPN allowlist; he prefers us to submit a single consolidated allowlist file and a short runbook for the connection test.
- I'll attach our security questionnaire — see attached (edgescale-security-questionnaire.pdf).

Kickoff availability: Tuesday 2027-06-22 at 10:00am PT works for the product + infra folks. Sam will be on the ops call.

One ask on metrics: can you add a short column in the metrics sheet for "tolerance" (acceptable deviation) so leadership can rapidly sign off?

On the model: we have an in-house distilled variant we'd like to test. Karthik — can your team accept a trimmed checkpoint (quantized) or do you prefer us to supply inference-ready weights?

Quote: "On Mon, Jun 14, 2027 at 3:20 PM, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com> wrote:"
> Key pain points you reiterated:
> - Latency spikes during burst traffic causing tail latency above acceptable SLAs (customer-facing inference).
> - Unpredictable per-token cost with current provider and lack of visibility by route/model.

Attachments: edgescale-security-questionnaire.pdf (attached)

—Emma
Product Lead | EdgeScale, Inc.
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Ross <emma@edgescale.com>, Sam Jensen <sam.jensen@edgescale.com>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: priorities, pilot scope & provisioning asks

Emma / Sam — appreciate the quick turnaround. Quick operational notes and a proposed checklist to reduce friction during Week 1 provisioning.

Provisioning checklist (ops):
1) Network allowlist: please confirm the egress IPs you can add; attach network-allowlist.txt we referenced. We will also provide a short TCP/UDP port matrix for the connection test.
2) Credentials: SFTP credentials for the anonymized logs. If you prefer presigned S3, tell us the bucket+path and we’ll pull.
3) Checkpoint format: we support standard PT/ONNX artifacts and can accept inference-ready weights. If you send a trimmed checkpoint, please include the tokenizer + config. We can run a smoke test on Day 1.
4) Access: we'll need a service account for ingestion and a separate service account for telemetry read-only access (so we don't touch production data flows).

Operational runbook (short):
- Day 0: Redwood creates a dedicated environment and posts the IPs; your infra confirms allowlist and SFTP details.
- Day 1: Ingest sample logs, run baseline throughput and P99 latency tests (we'll send a short run command).
- Day 2-7: Baseline tuning + initial evals; we’ll share interim results in a shared Drive doc.

Attached: pilot-metrics-template.xlsx (we've added a "tolerance" column per Emma's ask). Please review and populate baseline numbers where you can.

Question for EdgeScale: do you have any encryption-at-rest requirements beyond standard KMS? Also — Sam, do you require an SSH jump host for the initial tests, or will simple allowlist suffice?

Thanks — Karthik (solutions eng).

Attachments: pilot-metrics-template.xlsx (stub)

Acceptance criteria reminder (for quick signoff at end of pilot):
- P99 latency < 600ms for the prioritized prompt families under the agreed traffic profile.
- Token cost within the tolerance column of the metrics sheet.
- No unresolved critical security issues in the SOC2 evidence we exchange.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/RDW-3452), Pilot folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AExamplePilotDocs)

If anything shifts on your side, ping me and we’ll adjust timelines. Looking forward to the kickoff — we’ll keep the first week ops-heavy to remove friction so your product team can focus on evals.

Cheers,
Lukas Meyer
